claims.text: Threshold point first: the three artifacts describe one and the same trip, so the rider's initial burden under POL-RD-08(a) is discharged and this case is triable rather than dismissible on identity. EV-TRIP-00529, EV-GPS-00529 and EV-FARE-00529 each carry trip_id TRP-00529; the trace's first fix opens at 2026-09-17T18:31:40+08:00, exactly the trip record's started_at, and its last fix at 18:55:40 precedes the fare ledger's charged_at of 18:56:00. The pickup and dropoff timestamps are consistent across all three, and no artifact's timestamps run backwards.

The driver's own trace is complete and is not impaired for policy purposes on any limb of POL-RD-07: it carries 145 fixes at a 10-second cadence over a 100% coverage window, with no gaps at all (max_gap_sec 0.0, gaps empty), no straight-line jump exceeding 500 m, and a sustained sampling interval far below 30 seconds. Because limbs (a) to (c) of POL-RD-07 are not met, no POL-RD-07 consequence is triggered and there is no POL-GEN-02 discount to apply to any figure derived from this artifact: every derived number stands at its full weight of 1.0. That matters because POL-RD-01 makes gps_trace.trace_distance_km the governing measurement and expressly bars citation of the rounded trip_record.actual_distance_km for the threshold test — the platform's own trace, not a convenience copy, is the yardstick in this dispute.

The driver's answer to this dispute is that the clock ran because of traffic — 'meter waiting time is part of the fare, in every taxi in the world'. Nothing in the bundle supports that answer. The only traffic advisory in the pool, EV-ADVIS-00529-01, is MISSING: no payload, weight 0.0, and a BLOCKING MISSING_ARTIFACT issue code. I disclose that impairment expressly. POL-RD-03 exonerates only where an advisory names a road or segment the optimal route traverses, holds a validity window overlapping the time the trace shows the vehicle reaching that segment, and is matched by a route that leaves the optimal corridor and rejoins it — no such advisory exists for the Orchard Turn to Kim Seng Promenade corridor in this window, and the driver's trace, whose derived.deviation.status is 'no deviation', shows no corridor departure and rejoin at all. The alternative exculpatory route is equally empty: EV-CHAT-00529 records message_count 0 with no messages, so no rider instruction exists for POL-RD-04 either. Under POL-RD-08 a general assertion that traffic was bad, unsupported by a traffic_advisory ID, does not discharge the driver's burden.

The SGD 5.40 the rider contests is not distance at all. It sits in the metered time and waiting lines of EV-FARE-00529: a time_charge of SGD 6.72 for 24.0 charged minutes against a platform optimal duration of 9.0 minutes, and a waiting_time_fee of SGD 3.08 against a recorded wait of only 1.0 minute on the trip record. Whether those time-based lines are properly chargeable turns on whether the delay was an external event — and the only artifact that could evidence that, the traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-00529-01, is MISSING from this record at weight 0.0 with issue MISSING_ARTIFACT. A traffic justification asserted against an advisory that is missing from the pool is precisely the POL-RD-10(5) situation, and if the tribunal's confidence on those lines cannot reach the platform floor of 0.70, POL-RD-10(1) points the same way. The rider accordingly asks for ESCALATE rather than NO_ACTION, so that under POL-GEN-03 the disputed amount is held rather than collected and a human reviewer can determine what, if anything, justified the time and waiting charges.

Candour requires one concession and it narrows the rider's ask rather than inflating it. Measured as POL-RD-01 requires — on the trace, which governs — the excess is 0.11 km and 4.400% of the 2.5 km optimal, so neither the 0.8 km absolute gate nor the 20% proportional gate is passed, no route deviation is established, and the POL-RD-02 recomputation has nothing to run on. The rider does not press a distance refund. Nor is any pass-through correction available under POL-RD-09: the fare carries zero ERP gantries, zero tolls and a zero airport surcharge, and nothing in the ledger is a phantom line for a gantry the trace never crosses. The rider's complaint is confined to the time and waiting charges and to the driver's unsupported explanation for them.

Nothing on the rider's profile may be used against her, and the one profile field this category does allow is in her favour on its face: rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d is 0 and rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d_substantiated is 0, so the corroboration requirement that POL-RD-08 attaches to serial claimants is not triggered here and her account is not to be discounted on profile grounds. POL-GEN-01 confines every other field on either profile — rating, account age, lifetime trips, cancellation rate, prior counters — to context only, and the rider relies on none of them; the case must be decided on this trip's own trace, ledger and missing advisory.

The governing GPS trace measures this trip at 2.61 km against a booked optimal of 2.50 km — an excess of 0.11 km, or 4.4% of optimal. POL-RD-01 establishes a deviation only where the excess exceeds 20% of optimal AND exceeds 0.8 km in absolute terms; both gates fail here (4.4% is under 20%; 0.11 km is under 0.8 km), so no deviation exists on this record and the rider's route-deviation claim cannot be sustained.

POL-RD-01 makes the trace figure the governing measurement and expressly bars trip_record.actual_distance_km — a rounded convenience copy of the same measurement — from the threshold test. On the governing trace_distance_km of 2.61 km the excess is 0.11 km, less than one-seventh of the 0.8 km absolute gate, so the result does not turn on which of the two distance fields is read.

The rider carries the initial burden under POL-RD-08 and must show an excess meeting the POL-RD-01 threshold, measured from an unimpaired trace or from an independent source named in POL-RD-07(ii). The trace here is unimpaired on any limb of POL-RD-07: 145 fixes at a 10 second cadence, 100% coverage, no gaps and a maximum gap of 0.0 seconds. That clean trace shows an excess of 4.4%, so the burden is not discharged and the driver is never put to an exculpatory clause.

POL-RD-02 runs only 'where a deviation is established under POL-RD-01'. The refund figures published in the fare_breakdown's derived block (recomputed_fare 12.0750, refund before rounding 4.2750, payable 4.30) are conditional arithmetic computed on a deviation that this trip does not establish. Because the condition precedent fails, no refund figure is payable and the charge stands.

The rider's objection is that she 'didn't cause the traffic jam' and should not pay for it. What she is paying is the metered structure of a taxi trip: waiting_time_fee of 3.08 and time_fare of 6.72 on a 24.0 minute metered journey, both of which have counterparts on the trip record. POL-RD-02's own recomputation carries fare_breakdown.waiting_time_fee as a properly chargeable component of the fare, and POL-GEN-03 provides that where the evidence does not support the filing party's claim the present payment state stands.

There is no billing-integrity fallback available to the rider in this bundle: erp_gantries and erp_lines are both empty, the off-optimal-route ERP total is 0.00, and no airport surcharge line is applied on a trip that neither originates nor ends at an airport. POL-RD-09(4) therefore has no phantom gantry or misapplied surcharge to refund, and the four cents of rounding below the de minimis threshold of SGD 0.50 cannot found a payment.

The driver's trailing record shows no repeat-deviation pattern. driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 across 250 completed_trips_90d, below both POL-RD-06 thresholds, and no material deviation is recorded on this trip in any event. POL-RD-06 therefore licenses neither a FULL_REFUND uplift nor a driver-conduct referral on this record, and POL-GEN-01 confines the profiles to the single test each clause names.

Every artifact that decides this case is COMPLETE at weight_multiplier 1.0 — the GPS trace, the trip record and the payments ledger — and all three carry the same trip identifier TRP-00529 with mutually consistent timestamps and no sampling gaps. None of the POL-RD-10 triggers fires, and confidence in a NO_ACTION outcome is not capped below the 0.70 platform floor.

The rider's traffic-jam characterisation has no documentary support: the only traffic advisory artifact for this trip, EV-ADVIS-00529-01, is MISSING, carrying issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT and weight_multiplier 0.0, so it carries no fact and its absence is itself citable. POL-RD-01 disposes of the matter 'however the rider characterises the trip' once the two establishment gates fail, and the driver neither needs nor invokes any exoneration clause.

ruling.explanation: The fare stands and no money moves. This was a 2.5 km booking (ION Orchard to Great World) on a METERED taxi fare, and the platform's own GPS trace measures the driven route at 2.61 km — 0.11 km, or 4.4%, more than the booked optimal of 2.5 km. POL-RD-01 establishes a route deviation only where the excess is BOTH more than 0.8 km absolute AND more than 20% of optimal. Both gates fail (0.11 < 0.8; 4.4% < 20%), and POL-RD-01 requires the governing figure to be the trace, not the rounded 2.6 km convenience copy on the trip record — the result is the same on either. No deviation being established, POL-RD-02 never runs, so the conditional refund arithmetic in the fare breakdown (recomputed fare 12.0750, refund before rounding 4.2750, payable 4.30) is not payable. There is likewise no billing-integrity refund under POL-RD-09(4): the fare carries no ERP gantries, no tolls and no airport surcharge, so there is no phantom line to correct. What the rider is paying beyond the 3.80 flagfall and distance is the metered time structure — a time charge of 6.72 for 24.0 metered minutes at 0.28/min and a waiting_time_fee of 3.08 — and the policy treats the waiting fee as a properly chargeable component of a metered fare. A traffic jam, even one the rider did not cause, is not a refund ground: POL-RD-03 itself, where an external event exonerates a detour, expressly leaves the distance and time charges standing. On the rider's request for ESCALATE: POL-RD-10(5) fires only where a party invokes an exculpatory clause against a cited artifact that is missing from the pool. The driver invoked no exculpatory clause here and needed none, because no deviation was ever established and the driver's burden under POL-RD-08 never arose; a bare assertion that traffic was bad, citing no evidence, is discarded under POL-RD-08's burden rule, and a discarded assertion is not an escalation ground. POL-RD-10(1) does not fire either: the facts this ruling rests on — the GPS trace, the trip record and the payments ledger — are all COMPLETE at weight_multiplier 1.0, and all three carry trip_id TRP-00529 with consistent timestamps, so confidence is not capped below the 0.70 floor. The only impaired artifact, traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-00529-01, is MISSING at weight 0.0 with issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT; its absence is citable, as both sides rightly say, but it carries no fact and this ruling does not rest on it. The empty chat log (EV-CHAT-00529, 0 messages) means no rider-requested detour can be run under POL-RD-04, and none is needed. No referral issues: POL-RD-06(c) requires a repeat deviation pattern, and the driver's record shows deviation_flags_90d 0 across 250 completed trips in 90 days, so neither the FULL_REFUND uplift nor a conduct referral is licensed. Both profiles were used only for the tests their clauses name (deviation_claims_60d on the rider's side, deviation_flags_90d/completed_trips_90d on the driver's); neither party's rating, account age, lifetime trips or cancellation rate was used, and the rider's own claim that the rating field is context-only is correct.

To both parties — this ruling concerns trip TRP-00529 (ION Orchard to Great World, 17 Sep 2026) and the SGD 5.40 the rider contests.

ROUTE DEVIATION — NOT ESTABLISHED. POL-RD-01 requires the excess over the booked optimal to exceed 20% of optimal AND 0.8 km in absolute terms, measured on the GPS trace, which governs over the trip record's rounded copy. The trace is clean: 145 fixes at a 10-second cadence, 100% coverage, no gaps and a maximum gap of 0.0 s. It measures the trip at 2.61 km against an optimal of 2.50 km — an excess of 0.11 km, or 4.400%. Both gates fail (4.400% < 20%; 0.11 km < 0.8 km), so no deviation exists and POL-RD-01 directs NO_ACTION however the trip is characterised. The trip record's 2.60 km 'actual' is a rounded convenience copy of the same measurement and could not change that result.

WHY THE TIME AND WAITING CHARGES STAND. The trip took 24.0 minutes against a platform optimal of 9.0 minutes, at recorded speeds of 4.6-8.2 km/h — a slow trip, consistent with the congestion the rider mentions. But fare_breakdown.fare_model is METERED. The contested money sits in the metered time and waiting lines of EV-FARE-00529: time_fare SGD 6.72 for 24.0 charged minutes and waiting_time_fee SGD 3.08, within a charged_total of SGD 16.35. Under this policy the waiting-time fee is a properly chargeable component of a metered fare — POL-RD-02's own recomputation carries it — and the metered model charges for time spent in the vehicle. "I didn't cause the traffic jam" is not a ground for a refund under this policy. The POL-RD-02 figures on the ledger (recomputed_fare SGD 12.075, refund before rounding SGD 4.275) are conditional arithmetic computed on a deviation this trip does not establish, so nothing is payable from them. POL-RD-09 has nothing to refund either: no ERP gantries, no tolls, no airport surcharge, hence no billing-integrity defect.

WHY THIS IS DECIDED, NOT ESCALATED. The rider asks for ESCALATE on the ground that the driver's explanation ('meter waiting time is part of the fare'; 'taxis charge for jams') needs a traffic advisory, and the only one in the pool, EV-ADVIS-00529-01, is MISSING at weight 0.0 with issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT. I do not escalate. POL-RD-10(5) fires when an exculpatory clause is invoked against a missing artifact; no exculpatory clause was invoked here — the driver claimed no road closure and no route exoneration, and POL-RD-03 has nothing to exonerate because no deviation exists. The missing advisory is therefore noted (its absence is itself citable, and it carries no fact) but decides nothing. The other POL-RD-10 triggers do not fire: the trace is unimpaired under POL-RD-07(a)-(c); trip identifiers and timestamps match across trip record, trace and ledger; there is no charge line without a counterpart; and the two sides' evidence is not in contradiction of comparable strength. POL-RD-10(1) does not bite, as the ruling rests entirely on artifacts at weight_multiplier 1.0.

NO REFERRAL. POL-RD-06 was consulted: driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 over 250 completed_trips_90d, so no repeat-deviation pattern is established, no FULL_REFUND uplift applies, and no driver-conduct referral is produced. No other clause produces a referral. Both parties' profiles were used only as credibility context (POL-GEN-01); the rider's deviation_claims_60d is 0, so no additional corroboration was required of her.

OUTCOME. NO_ACTION. The charge stands as billed (payment_status CHARGED, refund_issued_sgd 0.00); nothing is refunded to the rider and nothing is paid to the driver. Confidence 0.95 — every artifact this ruling rests on carries weight 1.0, above the 0.70 floor.

Rider and driver: the route-deviation claim is not made out. POL-RD-01 requires excess distance greater than 20% of optimal and greater than 0.8 km. The governing GPS trace measures 2.61 km against the booked optimal of 2.50 km, an excess of 0.11 km, or 4.4%. Both gates fail, so no deviation is established. The trip record's 2.6 km is a rounded copy of the same measurement and cannot be used for the threshold test. Because no deviation is established, the fare breakdown's conditional arithmetic — recomputed_fare $12.0750, refund before rounding $4.2750, payable $4.30 — never becomes payable. The time fare of $6.72 for 24.0 charged minutes and the waiting-time fee of $3.08 are metered fare components itemised on the fare breakdown; the policy does not make them refundable merely because the trip took longer than the optimal 9.0 minutes. The rider's escalation request is rejected: the missing traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-00529-01 (weight 0.0, issue MISSING_ARTIFACT) carries no fact, and its absence does not force escalation because no exculpatory clause is invoked against it — the driver's position is that no deviation exists, not that a closure excused one. There is no billing-integrity correction: no ERP, toll, or airport surcharge is charged. The in-app call after the trip does not produce a referral; POL-RD-06(c) requires a repeat deviation pattern, and driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 across 250 completed_trips_90d. Confidence is 0.95, above the 0.70 floor, because the deciding artifacts — the GPS trace, trip record, and fare breakdown — each carry weight 1.0. The disputed charge stands.

Both parties: the outcome is NO_ACTION. The SGD 16.35 charged on EV-FARE-00529 stands; no refund and no driver payment issue, and no referral is added.

Rider — why your claim does not succeed. Your complaint is really about time lost in slow traffic, but the instrument that decides a route-deviation claim is the GPS trace, and it does not show a deviation. POL-RD-01 requires the driven distance to exceed the booked optimal by more than 20% AND by more than 0.8 km. The governing trace (EV-GPS-00529, complete, weight 1.0) measures 2.61 km against the booked optimal of 2.50 km on EV-TRIP-00529 — an excess of 0.11 km, or 4.4%. Neither gate is close. POL-RD-01 therefore directs NO_ACTION however the trip is characterised. The trace is not impaired (145 fixes at 10-second cadence, 100% coverage, maximum gap 0.0 s); its speeds of 4.6–8.2 kph show a slow crawl, not a detour, so this is a definite finding rather than an undecided one.

Consequences. Because no deviation is established, POL-RD-02 never runs, and the conditional figures in the fare ledger (recomputed_fare 12.0750, refund before rounding 4.2750, payable 4.30) are arithmetic on a deviation this trip does not have; nothing is payable on them. The time_fare of 6.72 (24.0 metered minutes at 0.28/min) and the waiting_time_fee of 3.08 are the metered structure of a taxi journey, not a route deviation, and POL-RD-02 itself carries the waiting fee as a properly chargeable component. There is no billing-integrity correction either: the fare carries no ERP gantries, no tolls and no airport surcharge (erp_lines total 0.00), so POL-RD-09(4) has nothing to refund.

Your escalation request. I have considered it and it is not available. POL-RD-10(5) escalates where a party invokes an exculpatory clause against an artifact missing from the pool; the driver invoked no exoneration clause — his position is that the meter ran and that waiting time is part of every taxi fare — and there is no deviation for any such clause to excuse, so the absent traffic advisory (EV-ADVIS-00529-01, MISSING, weight 0.0, issue MISSING_ARTIFACT) leaves no limb untested and changes nothing. That artifact can carry no fact, and a traffic characterisation does not become a ground of recovery merely because an advisory is absent. POL-RD-10(1) is also not met: the facts that decide this case rest on the GPS trace, the trip record and the fare ledger, all complete at weight 1.0, so confidence is well above the 0.70 floor.

Driver. Your position is accepted. No deviation is established on the trace, the rider's initial burden under POL-RD-08 fails (and POL-RD-08 confirms a general assertion that traffic was bad, unsupported by an advisory ID, shifts no burden), and you were never put to an exculpatory clause. No driver compensation is due: the billed distance (2.6 km) is not less than the trace distance (2.61 km), so POL-RD-04's compensation limb is not engaged.

Neither profile decides anything. POL-GEN-01 confines both profiles to the tests that name their fields; the rider's deviation_claims_60d is 0, so no extra corroboration is required of her, and no context-only field (rating, account age, lifetime trips, or any prior counter) has been used against either party. Your record shows 0 deviation flags in 90 days across 250 completed trips, so POL-RD-06 establishes no pattern, no FULL_REFUND uplift applies, and no driver-conduct referral issues. The rider's account of a post-trip call is noted; no clause produces a referral for it on this record, because POL-RD-06(c) requires a repeat-deviation pattern your profile does not show. Confidence in this ruling is 0.90.
